origins: Slower thinking, trouble finding words, and forgetfulness after injury or illness can feel humiliating, especially to those once quick and capable. Others’ impatience can deepen shame.
teaches: “The foolishness of God is wiser than man’s wisdom, and the weakness of God is stronger than man’s strength” (1 Corinthians 1:25). “For the LORD gives wisdom; from His mouth come knowledge and understanding” (Proverbs 2:6). “The unfolding of Your words gives light; it informs the simple” (Psalm 119:130). Wisdom is more than speed: it includes humility, kindness, faith, and love. Your intelligence is one part of you, and it is not the source of your worth.
self_statements: Everyone sees how slow I am.
I make mistakes all the time.
errors: Believing I am either smart or stupid.
Predicting that I will always struggle.
Feeling slow and concluding I am stupid.
questions: What can I still do well?
How has my thinking changed, and what helps?
What strategies, like lists, routines, and extra time, help?
What qualities of wisdom do I still have?
What would I say to a friend who had the same injury?
Whom can I ask for patience and help?
truth: I am not stupid. My thinking has changed, and I can use tools and patient help. Wisdom is a gift from God that includes more than speed. My worth is secure.
hw_truths: I am fearfully and wonderfully made.
I can use tools that help.
log: Each week, note one thing you handled well.
actions: Ask for more time without apology.
prayer: Lord, my mind feels slow. Give me wisdom, patience, and tools that help, and remind me that my worth is in You. Amen.
